title: Keep source code parseable
description: Make sure every analyzed file is valid source code. CodeDNA measures the share of files that cannot be parsed because of syntax errors; such files cannot be measured at all.
objective: No files with syntax errors in the analyzed source.

steps.title: Understand why syntax errors matter
steps.description: A file that does not parse cannot be compiled, run or measured. Syntax errors in a repository often come from unfinished edits, merge conflict markers, or files that are not really source code, such as templates or generated fragments.
steps.objective: Know the common sources of unparseable files.

steps.title: Find the files that do not parse
steps.description: Use the syntax error findings of your latest analysis, which name the file and line, to list every file that failed to parse.
steps.objective: A complete list of unparseable files.

steps.title: Fix invalid syntax
steps.description: Fix each error at the reported line. Remove conflict markers and dead fragments, and exclude files that are not source code from the archive you upload.
steps.objective: Every listed file parses, or is no longer uploaded.

steps.title: Validate before you upload
steps.description: Run your language's parser, compiler or linter over the whole project, locally or in CI, so that syntax errors are caught before an analysis.
steps.objective: An automatic syntax check for the whole project.

steps.title: Complete a code hygiene challenge
steps.description: Practise on a short coding challenge for this competency. It is checked by deterministic tests and structural rules in an isolated sandbox.
steps.objective: Repair a small file so that it parses and behaves as specified.

steps.title: Re-assess with a new analysis
steps.description: Upload the fixed source and run a new CodeDNA analysis. Only a new analysis can show whether the measured code hygiene changed.
steps.objective: A new analysis of the fixed code.
